DK.name: Denmark
DK.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
DK.passport: Passport, driving licence or ID card with travel rights accepted (Nordic passport freedom)
DK.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; border checks with Germany listed to 11 Nov 2026, may be extended
DK.notes: Norwegian MFA Denmark (updated 5 May 2026): passport, driving licence or ID card with travel rights; Nordic passport freedom, but be able to show you are a Nordic citizen. EC list: temporary border control at the German land and sea border 12 Jul-11 Nov 2026 (may be extended). Only the red-label ID card has travel rights. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay (MFA pages for DE, AT, PT, HR give the same 3-month threshold).

SE.name: Sweden
SE.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
SE.passport: ID card or passport; be ready to show you are a Nordic citizen (Nordic passport freedom)
SE.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; border checks on all internal borders to 11 May 2027, carry ID
SE.notes: Norwegian MFA Sweden (updated 1 Jun 2026) only describes Nordic passport freedom and does not mention the ID card; ID card validity in the EU/EEA and Switzerland comes from the MFA Q&A page. EC list: Swedish temporary border control on all internal borders 12 May-11 Nov 2026, then 12 Nov 2026-11 May 2027. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

FI.name: Finland
FI.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
FI.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; carry one even between Nordic countries
FI.notes: Norwegian MFA Finland (updated 22 Jun 2026): passport freedom in the Nordics, but you may be asked to prove you are a Nordic citizen, so carry passport or ID card; the page repeats that the red-label card is valid as a travel document in the EU/EEA and Switzerland. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

EE.name: Estonia
EE.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
EE.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid the whole trip; driving licence/bank card not enough
EE.notes: Norwegian MFA Estonia (updated 31 Mar 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights must be carried even though Estonia is in Schengen; driving licence and bank card are not enough; the document must be valid for the whole trip. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

LV.name: Latvia
LV.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
LV.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid for the whole trip
LV.notes: Norwegian MFA Latvia (updated 29 Apr 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights is required for entry and exit and must be valid for the whole trip; driving licence and bank card are not travel documents. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

LT.name: Lithuania
LT.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
LT.passport: Passport or ID card; several airlines and ferry operators insist on one of them
LT.notes: Norwegian MFA Lithuania (updated 17 Sep 2026): Schengen member, no visa; several airlines and ferry companies require a valid passport or ID card. Vilnius airport has been closed at times by balloons from Belarus (affects flights, not entry rules). 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

PL.name: Poland
PL.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
PL.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; carry valid ID at all times in Poland
PL.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; border checks at the German and Lithuanian borders to 30 Mar 2027
PL.notes: Norwegian MFA Poland (page updated 25 Sep 2025, older): valid ID for Norwegians means passport or national ID card with travel rights; carry it at all times. EC list: temporary border control at the German and Lithuanian land borders 2 Oct 2026-30 Mar 2027. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

DE.name: Germany
DE.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
DE.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; need only be valid until your departure day
DE.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; checks at all German land borders to 15 Mar 2027, carry your ID
DE.notes: Norwegian MFA Germany (updated 27 May 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights; the document need only be valid until your departure day; registration with German authorities only for stays over 3 months. Border control at all land borders (EC list: 16 Sep 2026-15 Mar 2027). 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
CZ.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; carry one at all times
CZ.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; the EES registration does not apply to Norwegians
CZ.notes: Norwegian MFA Czechia (updated 27 May 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights; the EU Entry/Exit System registration at Czech airports does not apply to citizens of EU countries, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein or Switzerland (EC: EES fully operational since 10 Apr 2026 for non-EU nationals). Reporting duty after 30 days' stay. 90 days = EEA 3-month stay.

AT.name: Austria
AT.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
AT.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; carry one at all times
AT.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; border checks with SK, CZ, HU, SI to 15 Mar 2027, carry your ID
AT.notes: Norwegian MFA Austria (page updated 22 Feb 2024, older): passport or ID card with travel rights is the only valid ID for Norwegians; registration needed only for stays over 3 months. EC list: temporary border control with Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Slovenia 16 Sep 2026-15 Mar 2027. 90 days = EEA 3-month stay.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
HU.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid for the whole stay
HU.notes: Norwegian MFA Hungary (updated 20 May 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights, valid for the whole stay; the green-label card has no travel rights. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
SK.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights
SK.notes: Norwegian MFA Slovakia (page last updated 12 Jun 2023, old): passport or ID card with travel rights; only the red-label card has travel rights. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay. The page is old, so the generic MFA Q&A statement carries the ID-card rule.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
NL.passport: Passport or national ID card, valid for the whole stay
NL.notes: Norwegian MFA Netherlands (updated 3 Jun 2026): passport and national ID card are the only valid travel documents for Norwegians and must be valid for the whole stay. The Netherlands is not on the EC list of temporary border controls. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
BE.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; Belgium has a legal duty to carry ID
BE.notes: Norwegian MFA Belgium (page updated 4 Jun 2024, older): passport or ID card with travel rights; Belgium has an ID duty, so always carry a valid Norwegian travel document. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
LU.passport: Passport or national ID card; hotels often ask for the passport at check-in
LU.notes: Norwegian MFA Luxembourg (page updated 19 Dec 2024, older): passport and national ID card are the only valid travel documents; hotels often require a passport at check-in; there is no passport control to or from Luxembourg, but airlines and security may still ask for ID. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.paperwork: Get a UK ETA in the UK ETA app or on gov.uk before you travel (£20, about €24). Valid 2 years; ID card not accepted.
GB.passport: Passport valid for the whole stay; the ETA is linked to it. Norwegian ID card is not accepted
GB.atBorder: Passport only; wait for the ETA confirmation email before you travel
GB.notes: Fee rose from £16 to £20 on 8 Apr 2026 (gov.uk). gov.uk: decision usually within a day but can take up to 3 working days; an ETA lasts 2 years or until the passport expires; up to 6 months per visit. Needed also for airside transit if you leave the transit area (Norwegian MFA, 7 Oct 2026). A machine-readable passport is needed; emergency passports need a visa. A Norwegian ID card only works for people with UK residence status. Use only gov.uk or the official app; lookalike sites charge more.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough. No visa, ETA or fee; Ireland is outside Schengen.
IE.passport: Passport (emergency passport accepted) or ID card with travel rights, valid for the stay
IE.notes: Norwegian MFA Ireland (updated 10 Mar 2026): valid passport (including emergency passport) or national ID card with travel rights; no visa. Ireland is EU but not Schengen, so expect an ID check on arrival. The Irish immigration page (irishimmigration.ie) could not be read in full. 90 days = EU/EEA 3-month stay without registering (Your Europe); not stated on the MFA page.

FR.name: France
FR.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
FR.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, checked on entry and exit
FR.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; border checks with neighbours to 30 Apr 2027, carry your ID
FR.notes: Norwegian MFA France (updated 10 Oct 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights, shown on entry and exit; the green-label card has no travel rights. EC list: temporary border control with BE, DE, LU, CH, ES and IT 1 May-31 Oct 2026, renewed 1 Nov 2026-30 Apr 2027. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

ES.name: Spain
ES.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
ES.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; need only be valid until departure
ES.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; Italy air/sea checks listed to 22 Oct 2026, may be extended
ES.notes: Norwegian MFA Spain (updated 10 Aug 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights, need not be valid beyond your departure day; hotels and car-rental firms must collect personal data from guests. EC list: temporary controls on air and sea links with Italy in 2-week periods to 22 Oct 2026. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
PT.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; need only be valid until departure
PT.notes: Norwegian MFA Portugal (updated 3 Jun 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights; need not be valid beyond departure; Norwegians must register with Portuguese authorities only for stays over three months. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

IT.name: Italy
IT.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
IT.passport: Passport, emergency passport or ID card with travel rights
IT.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; checks at the Slovenian land border run to 18 Dec 2026
IT.notes: Norwegian MFA Italy (updated 29 Sep 2026): passport, emergency passport or ID card with travel rights are the only valid travel documents. EC list: temporary border control at the Slovenian land border 19 Jun-18 Dec 2026 and at air/sea links with Spain 1-16 Oct 2026. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

GR.name: Greece
GR.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
GR.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; need only be valid until departure
GR.notes: Norwegian MFA Greece (updated 30 Jul 2026): passport (emergency passport accepted) or ID card with travel rights; need not be valid beyond departure. No tourist registration required. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

MT.name: Malta
MT.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
MT.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; show on request and at hotel check-in
MT.notes: Norwegian MFA Malta (updated 3 Jun 2026): passport/emergency passport or ID card with travel rights are the only valid travel documents; you must be able to present one on request and at hotel or Airbnb check-in. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee; Cyprus is outside Schengen.
CY.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; not needed beyond the planned departure day
CY.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; read the MFA note before crossing to the north
CY.notes: Norwegian MFA Cyprus (updated 30 Jul 2026): passport or ID card with travel rights; Cyprus is EU but not Schengen. No stay length or registration stated on the page; 90 days = EU/EEA 3-month rule (not stated by the MFA). Crossing to the Turkish-occupied north: Norway does not recognise it, there is no consular help there, and rental cars need extra insurance for the north.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.paperwork: Passport only. Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180; no form or fee. The old ID-card concession ended on 31 Dec 2022.
TR.passport: Valid at least 150 days after arrival (60 days beyond the 90-day stay) and one blank page
TR.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; Norwegian ID cards are no longer accepted
TR.notes: Turkish MFA: Norwegian ordinary passports are visa-exempt 90 days in any 180; the chipped-ID-card provision for Norwegians applied only until 31 Dec 2022 (temporary, direct flights, 6 months validity). Norwegian MFA (12 Oct 2026): passport is the only valid ID for Norwegians; the page still links an outdated 2022 news item 'Nasjonalt ID-kort gir innreise til Tyrkia'. The Turkish MFA page listing ID-card countries did not mention Norway (page content partial). Passport rule: expiry at least 60 days beyond the visa-free stay, so 150 days from arrival.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
BG.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid beyond your planned departure day
BG.notes: Norwegian MFA Bulgaria (updated 7 Oct 2026): full Schengen member since 1 Jan 2025 (EC confirms Bulgaria and Romania joined last on that date); passport, emergency passport or ID card with travel rights, valid beyond the planned departure day. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

RO.name: Romania
RO.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
RO.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid beyond your planned departure day
RO.notes: Norwegian MFA Romania (updated 7 Oct 2026): full Schengen member since 1 Jan 2025; passport, emergency passport or ID card with travel rights, valid beyond your planned departure day. 90 days = EEA 3-month free-movement stay.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
HR.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; be able to identify yourself on request
HR.notes: Norwegian MFA Croatia (updated 14 Aug 2026): passport, emergency passport and ID card with travel rights are valid; Schengen since 1 Jan 2023; police registration only for stays over 3 months. The page says Slovenia has border control towards Croatia until 21 Dec 2026, but MFA Slovenia (16 Jun 2026) says it ended and the EC list shows none for Slovenia - treat as uncertain. 90 days = EEA 3-month stay.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
SI.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights, valid for the whole stay
SI.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; carry valid ID for any checks
SI.notes: Norwegian MFA Slovenia (updated 16 Jun 2026): passport (emergency passport accepted) or ID card with travel rights, valid for the whole stay; temporary border control towards Croatia and Hungary ended in June 2026, but travellers must still show valid ID at any checks (the EC list shows no Slovenian controls). 90 days = EEA 3-month stay.

RS.name: Serbia
RS.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough for up to 90 days. No visa or fee.
RS.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; the MFA page gives no minimum validity
RS.atBorder: Private lodging: register with local police within 24 h; declare cash over €10,000
RS.notes: Norwegian MFA Serbia (updated 1 Oct 2026): valid Norwegian passport (emergency passport accepted) or national ID card with travel rights; visa-free up to 90 days. Without the 'Registration of place of stay' document you may have trouble leaving. You cannot enter Serbia from Kosovo unless you entered Kosovo from Serbia; people with Kosovo background may be questioned. Serbia's own MFA page (mfa.gov.rs) was not read.

AL.name: Albania
AL.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough for up to 90 days in 6 months. No visa or fee.
AL.passport: Passport valid 3 months from entry, or ID card with travel rights
AL.notes: Norwegian MFA Albania (updated 26 Aug 2026): no visa; 90 days within a six-month period; passport valid three months from entry (emergency passport accepted); 'national ID card with travel rights is also sufficient for entry'. Drones must be registered. Albania's own immigration site was not read.

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BA.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough for up to 90 days. No visa or fee.
BA.passport: Passport or ID card valid at least 3 months after your planned departure
BA.notes: Norwegian MFA Bosnia and Herzegovina (updated 14 Aug 2026): both passport and national ID card with travel rights are valid for entry; visa-free up to 90 days; travel document valid at least three months after planned departure. No registration or fee mentioned. The country's own authorities were not read.

MK.name: North Macedonia
MK.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough for up to 90 days. No visa or fee.
MK.passport: Passport or ID card valid at least 3 months after your planned departure
MK.atBorder: Private lodging: register with local police within 24 h; declare cash over €10,000
MK.notes: Norwegian MFA North Macedonia (updated 15 May 2026): passport (emergency passport accepted) or national ID card with travel rights; 90 days visa-free; passport valid three months from planned departure; cash over €10,000 must be declared on entry and exit. Drone flying is regulated. Own authorities not read.

ME.name: Montenegro
ME.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough. Entry on the ID card gives 30 days, on a passport 90 days.
ME.passport: Passport or ID card valid at least 3 months after your planned departure
ME.atBorder: Private lodging: register with local police within 24 h; declare cash over €10,000
ME.notes: Norwegian MFA Montenegro (updated 15 May 2026): 'up to 90 days (entry with passport)'; the page says ID-card entry allows 30 days, which still covers an 8-night trip. Passport valid three months from planned departure; emergency passport accepted; police registration within 24 h for private accommodation; cash over €10,000 must be declared. Own authorities not read.

XK.name: Kosovo
XK.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough. Register your address online within 3 days of arrival.
XK.passport: Passport or ID card valid at least 3 months after your planned departure
XK.atBorder: Address registration in Kosovo's digital system within 3 days (foreign visitors, since 15 March)
XK.notes: Norwegian MFA Kosovo (updated 9 Sep 2026): no visa, 90 days within six months; ID card with travel rights is sufficient. Since 15 March (year not stated, presumably 2026) foreign visitors must register their address digitally within three days after arrival; the page does not say whether hotels do it automatically. Level is 'form' rather than 'id' only because of this free registration, which happens after arrival, not before the trip. You cannot go from Kosovo straight into Serbia unless you entered Kosovo from Serbia; route via North Macedonia. Own authorities not read.

MD.name: Moldova
MD.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (with travel rights) or passport is enough for up to 90 days in 180. No visa or fee.
MD.passport: Passport or ID card valid at least 3 months beyond your planned departure
MD.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; the MFA advises against travel to Transnistria
MD.notes: Norwegian MFA Moldova (header date 24 Aug 2026, body also shows 26 Jul 2022): 'passport or national ID card with travel rights' and passport valid three months beyond planned departure. The Moldovan MFA visa-exemption list (mfa.gov.md) names the Kingdom of Norway but does not state the stay length or ID-card rule; the 90-days-in-180 rule and the ID-card marker for Norway come from Wikipedia and the Norwegian MFA text. The Norwegian MFA text does not state the visa-free stay for ordinary passports. Security: drone incidents and power cuts (MFA).

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
CH.passport: Passport or ID card with travel rights; carry ID at all times
CH.notes: Norwegian MFA Switzerland (updated 29 Apr 2026): valid passport (emergency passport accepted) or national ID card with travel rights; Switzerland is in Schengen. No maximum stay is stated; 90 days is the EFTA/EEA 3-month rule, not confirmed on a Swiss page. The page also says several European countries still run temporary border control and demand a passport, so carry your passport as a backup.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.paperwork: Norwegian national ID card (red label, with travel rights) or passport is enough. No form, visa or fee.
IS.passport: Passport recommended; ID card accepted; some airlines prefer passport or ID card
IS.notes: Norwegian MFA Iceland (updated 9 Aug 2026): in principle you can travel without a passport in the Nordics, but the MFA recommends a passport and says some airlines prefer passport or national ID card. ID card with travel rights is valid across the EEA (MFA Q&A). 90 days = EEA 3-month stay (not stated on the page).

FO.name: Faroe Islands
FO.paperwork: Nordic citizens need only photo ID (Norwegian ID card, passport or similar). No passport, form, visa or fee.
FO.passport: Passport not required for Nordic citizens, but a photo identity document is
FO.atBorder: Be ready to show you are a Nordic citizen; the Faroes are outside Schengen but Nordics enter freely
FO.notes: Official Faroese tourism site: Nordic citizens are not obliged to hold a passport but need a photo identity document, and may stay indefinitely without permits (no day limit, so stayDays is null). Danish Immigration Service: citizens of Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden can enter, reside and work in the Faroe Islands and Greenland without a permit. The Faroes are not in Schengen or the EU. The Norwegian MFA has no separate Faroe Islands page; its Denmark page (updated 5 May 2026) covers Nordic passport freedom. Airlines may apply their own ID rules (not checked).

MA.name: Morocco
MA.paperwork: Passport only. No visa for up to 90 days and no online form for Norwegians; officers often ask for your address.
MA.passport: Valid 6 months from entry (Moroccan rule, per Norwegian MFA)
MA.atBorder: Be ready to give your address in Morocco; drones need prior approval
MA.notes: Norwegian MFA Morocco (updated 21 Jul 2026): 90 days visa-free; passport valid six months from entry; no arrival form mentioned; e-visa fees (MAD 770/1,100) do not apply to Norwegians; extending past 90 days means contacting police within 15 days (fine MAD 1,000/day for overstay). Morocco has an electronic travel authorisation (AEVM) via acces-maroc.ma for some nationalities and Wikipedia says it may extend to all visa-exempt countries; Norway is not named, but check acces-maroc.ma before booking (the portal could not be read). ID card not mentioned as accepted.

TN.name: Tunisia
TN.paperwork: Passport only. No visa for up to 90 days; no online registration or fee mentioned.
TN.passport: Valid more than 3 months after entry date; emergency passports are not accepted
TN.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; photographing police or military sites is illegal
TN.notes: Norwegian MFA Tunisia (updated 16 Mar 2026): 90 days visa-free; passport rule (more than 3 months after entry) since 1 Jan 2025; handwritten emergency passports unusable from 25 Oct 2025. The MFA advises against travel to southern areas and the Algerian border region. No customs form or e-registration mentioned. ID card not mentioned as accepted. Tunisian authorities were not read.

EG.name: Egypt
EG.paperwork: Tourist visa needed: e-visa online (USD 30, apply 7+ days ahead) or visa on arrival (USD 30 cash). 30 days.
EG.passport: Machine-readable, valid at least 6 months after entry
EG.atBorder: Pay USD 30 cash for visa on arrival; free 15-day Sinai resort stamp only within town limits
EG.notes: Official e-visa portal: single-entry tourist visa USD 30, passport valid at least 6 months from arrival, create the e-visa application at least 7 days before departure (applyDaysAhead is 0 because visa on arrival is the no-advance route). Norwegian MFA (17 Sep 2026): visa on arrival USD 30 as of 1 Mar 2026 in cash (its Taba section still says USD 25); 15-day free entry for Sharm el-Sheikh, Dahab and Nuweiba only if you stay within the hotel area or town limits. Drones banned; max EGP 5,000 cash; foreign currency over USD 10,000 must be declared. MFA advises against North Sinai.

JO.name: Jordan
JO.paperwork: Visa needed: pay JOD 40 on arrival, or buy the Jordan Pass (JOD 70+) before arrival, which waives it for 2+ nights.
JO.passport: Valid at least 6 months after planned departure; emergency passports not accepted
JO.atBorder: Airport: pay JOD 40 or show Jordan Pass; land-border exit tax JOD 10 (not by air)
JO.notes: Jordan Pass FAQ: single-entry visa fee JOD 40 (about USD 60); passes cost JOD 70/75/80 and waive the visa fee if bought before arrival and you stay at least 2 whole nights; the FAQ also says non-restricted nationalities need no visa when arriving at Aqaba airport (only on the Jordan Pass site, not confirmed on a government page). Norwegian MFA (5 Oct 2026): e-visa via the Ministry of Interior, visa on arrival or Jordan Pass; passport valid 6 months after planned departure; land-border exit tax JOD 10; regional security unpredictable, airspace and the Jordan-Israel crossing can close at short notice. Stay length not confirmed: media report a rise from 30 to 90 days in Jan 2026, the MFA says extension up to ten weeks.

IL.name: Israel
IL.paperwork: Apply online for ETA-IL (NIS 25, about €7) at least 72 hours before departure; valid 2 years, up to 90 days per visit.
IL.passport: Israel: valid 3 months beyond arrival (ETA-IL); Norwegian MFA says 6 months after departure
IL.atBorder: Expect security questions; a one-way ticket can lead to refusal; the ETA does not guarantee entry
IL.notes: ETA-IL required for Norwegians since 1 Jan 2025; fee NIS 25 (MFA and PIBA via search extract); non-refundable; valid up to 2 years or until the passport expires. Passport: Israeli gov.il 'New Entry Requirement' page (via search extract) says 3 months beyond arrival for ETA travellers, the Norwegian MFA (29 Sep 2026) says 6 months after planned departure; use the stricter. PIBA and embassy pages are JavaScript/blocked, so timing (72 h before departure or booking) and rules come from search extracts. MFA: travellers with a one-way ticket may be refused; some travellers are refused for security reasons without explanation; advice against travel within 5 km of the Lebanon, Syria and Gaza borders; advisory lowered on 30 Jun 2026 after the Feb-Apr 2026 US-Iran war.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.paperwork: Passport only. No visa for up to 90 days in any 180; no form or fee for Norwegians.
AE.passport: Valid at least 6 months on arrival; only passports accepted (no ID card or emergency passport)
AE.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; medicines, drones and alcohol have strict rules
AE.notes: Norwegian MFA UAE (updated 14 Jul 2026): no visa needed, 90 days within 180; passport valid six months; the UAE accepts only passports (not ID cards or emergency passports). Wikipedia agrees (90 in 180, 6 months, no pre-registration). The MFA describes the Middle East security situation as unclear and fast-changing and lowered the UAE advisory on 24 Apr 2026. UAE official sites (u.ae, ICP) could not be read.

OM.name: Oman
OM.paperwork: Passport only for stays up to 14 days (Norway is on Oman's visa-free list). Bring return ticket, hotel booking and insurance.
OM.passport: Valid at least 6 months (Oman foreign ministry); the Norwegian MFA gives no figure
OM.atBorder: Return ticket, confirmed hotel booking, health insurance and funds; 14 days cannot be extended
OM.notes: Oman foreign ministry: Norway is in the first group of 100+ countries with 14-day visa-free entry; conditions are a return ticket, a confirmed hotel reservation, health insurance and enough money; the stay cannot be extended or converted; passport valid at least six months. Norwegian MFA (11 Oct 2026) calls it a free 14-day visa on arrival. Longer stay: 30-day tourist visa OMR 20 (about €46), bought on arrival or via evisa.rop.gov.om; 10-day visa OMR 10, on arrival only (MFA). MFA says the security situation in Oman is serious because of the regional conflict and flights may be affected. ROP e-visa pages were not readable.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.paperwork: Passport only. Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180; no visa, Hayya or other form needed for Norwegians.
QA.passport: Valid at least 3 months on arrival (MFA, Qatar MOI); some sources say 6, so carry 6+ months
QA.atBorder: Confirmed return ticket may be checked; health insurance needed only for stays over 30 days
QA.notes: Norwegian MFA Qatar (updated 14 Jul 2026): no visa up to 90 days in any 180; passport valid at least three months on arrival; only passports are accepted (no ID card); health insurance is required for stays over 30 days; alcohol, pork products and drugs may not be imported. Qatar MOI page: three months passport validity and a confirmed return ticket for the on-arrival framework, Hayya is the e-platform for tourist visa applications. Wikipedia lists Norway among free visa-on-arrival countries (90 days) and cites a 6-month passport rule; the MOI list of visa-exempt nationals did not load. MFA lowered the Qatar advisory on 24 Apr 2026.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.paperwork: Passport only for stays up to 1 year, no visa. Since 1 Jan 2026 you must hold travel insurance covering the whole stay.
GE.passport: Valid passport or emergency passport; the Norwegian MFA states no minimum validity
GE.atBorder: Show proof of travel insurance for the stay (reported minimum cover GEL 30,000)
GE.notes: Norwegian MFA Georgia (updated 26 Jun 2026): visa-free up to one year; 'from 1 January 2026 valid travel insurance is mandatory for all visitors' and must be shown on entry. Wikipedia: Decree No. 602 of 26 Dec 2025, minimum cover GEL 30,000 (about USD 11,000), valid for the stay; legal-news summaries say patrol police at the border check it and failure may mean refused entry (not on the MFA page). ID card not accepted (passport or emergency passport). MFA advises against Abkhazia and South Ossetia. Georgia's own consular site did not show the rule.

AM.name: Armenia
AM.paperwork: Passport only. Visa-free for up to 180 days per year; no form or fee.
AM.passport: Valid for the whole stay; the MFA says a Norwegian passport is required for entry
AM.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; the land borders with Türkiye and Azerbaijan are closed
AM.notes: Norwegian MFA Armenia (updated 12 Mar 2026, when it also adjusted the travel advice): no visa for up to 180 days per year; passport valid for the whole stay; Norwegian passport required for entry. The Armenian MFA visa-free list (mfa.am/en/visafreelist) confirms Norway (no. 29) may stay up to 180 days per year. The page says nothing on passport validity or ID cards. ID card not accepted.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
AZ.paperwork: Apply for the e-visa at evisa.gov.az (about USD 25) at least 3 working days ahead. No visa on arrival.
AZ.passport: Portal: valid 3 months beyond the e-visa's expiry; MFA says 6 months after entry - use 6
AZ.atBorder: Entry must be by air (MFA); stays over 15 days need registration with migration authorities
AZ.notes: Norwegian MFA Azerbaijan (updated 2 Jun 2026): visa required, not available at the border; e-visa at evisa.gov.az, normally 72 hours, up to 30 days within 90; not valid on emergency passports; entry by air only; exit by land not allowed without special permission. Fee is uncertain: Wikipedia says USD 25 including a USD 5 service fee (urgent USD 60); the Azerbaijani embassy in The Hague reportedly lists USD 20 standard and USD 50 urgent; a reseller shows USD 26. I used USD 25 (about €22); check the portal's payment page. Official portal text (via search extract): standard e-visa within 3 working days, apply at least 3 working days before arrival. The portal itself returned 403. MFA advises against Nagorno-Karabakh and areas within 5 km of the Armenian border.

CV.name: Cape Verde
CV.paperwork: Pre-register on EASE (ease.gov.cv) about 5 days before and pay the airport security tax CVE 3,400 (€31). Visa-free 30 days.
CV.passport: Valid at least 6 months after departure; emergency passport also accepted
CV.atBorder: Show the EASE confirmation; if unregistered you register and pay at the airport (queues)
CV.notes: Cabo Verde government FAQ: all travellers must pre-register (EASE); international airport security fee CVE 3,400 = EUR 30.83, paid through the pre-registration platform; those who did not pre-register register and pay on arrival (PARES). Norwegian MFA (3 Jun 2026): visa-free 30 days, register on EASE at the latest five days before travel, passport valid six months after departure. Visa on arrival ended 1 Jan 2026 for 96 nationalities (EASE site); Norway stays in the 30-day visa-free group (Wikipedia, MFA). One site says the penalty for arriving unregistered doubles from 1 Jul 2026 - unverified. Yellow fever certificate only if arriving from a risk area (MFA); FAQ says no vaccine required.

SN.name: Senegal
SN.paperwork: Visa needed: free visa on arrival at Dakar airport only (about 30 days). Land or sea arrivals need an embassy visa in advance.
SN.passport: Valid at least 6 months after entry, with 1-2 blank pages
SN.atBorder: Return ticket and proof of accommodation; yellow fever certificate if arriving from a risk area
SN.notes: Norwegian MFA Senegal (updated 25 Sep 2026): Norwegians need a visa; at Dakar airport it is issued free on arrival, in practice valid 30 days; longer stays, multiple entry or arrival by sea/land need advance application via the Senegalese embassy in The Hague. Wikipedia lists Norway as eligible for visa on arrival at Dakar only (1 month, passport 6 months, return ticket, accommodation proof). The Senegalese embassy in the UK describes a free visa on arrival at Dakar for 'A and B category' nationals (Norway not named). Some commercial sites say Norwegians are visa-free or need an e-visa; no official Senegalese source could be read, so the MFA statement is used. MFA also mentions a health declaration form and a vaccination certificate on arrival; malaria area. Classified 'visa' although free.

GM.name: Gambia
GM.paperwork: Passport only. No visa for up to 90 days; no form or fee, but a yellow fever vaccination card must be shown.
GM.passport: Valid 6 months beyond the end of the trip; emergency passport accepted
GM.atBorder: Yellow fever vaccination card is checked on entry (per Norwegian MFA)
GM.notes: Norwegian MFA Gambia (updated 8 May 2026): no visa for Norwegians up to 90 days; no e-visa or pre-registration mentioned; passport valid six months beyond the trip; yellow fever vaccination card must be shown on entry and the vaccine is required; malaria area. Wikipedia: EFTA citizens visa-free 90 days (cites Gambia Immigration, not read). The MFA suggests contacting the Gambian embassy in London for questions. ID card not mentioned as accepted.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.paperwork: Fill in the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 3 days before arrival. Visa-free 30 days since 15 Sep 2026.
TH.passport: Valid at least 6 months on arrival, without visible damage
TH.atBorder: May be asked for onward ticket within 30 days, accommodation and THB 10,000-20,000 in funds
TH.notes: Visa-free stay cut from 60 to 30 days from 15 Sep 2026 (Royal Gazette 31 Aug 2026; Norway is no. 40 of 60 countries on the Tourism Authority of Thailand list); extendable by 30 days at a local immigration office; land entries limited to twice per calendar year. TDAC: mandatory since 1 May 2025, free, submitted within 3 days before arrival and for every entry; use only tdac.immigration.go.th (the portal itself could not be read). Proof of funds: Thai embassy London says officers may ask for THB 20,000 per person (about €530) plus accommodation and onward travel within 30 days; TAT's 6 Jul 2026 reminder gives THB 10,000 for visa-exempt cases and says it is not a new rule. The planned THB 300 tourist entry fee had no confirmed start date in the latest reports (would be collected in air tickets). ID card not accepted.

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.paperwork: Submit the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online up to 3 days before arrival. Visa-free up to 90 days.
MY.passport: Valid at least 6 months on arrival; a Norwegian passport is required (no ID card)
MY.atBorder: Return or onward ticket and enough funds can be checked
MY.notes: Norwegian MFA Malaysia (updated 30 Apr 2026): no visa for tourist stays up to 90 days; passport valid six months on arrival; MDAC to be completed up to three days before planned arrival; return/onward ticket and sufficient funds are required. The MFA page states no MDAC fee; the 'free' status comes from the task brief and general knowledge, and the MDAC portal returned a certificate error, so it was not confirmed first-hand. Beware paid lookalike sites.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.paperwork: Submit the free SG Arrival Card online (with health declaration) within 3 days before arrival. Visa-free, normally up to 90 days.
SG.passport: Valid at least 6 months on arrival (Norwegian MFA)
SG.atBorder: Funds and onward ticket can be checked; false declarations are an offence
SG.notes: ICA: all travellers, including visa-free visitors, must submit the SG Arrival Card with electronic health declaration before arriving, up to three days before arrival (counting arrival day); free; transit passengers without immigration clearance are exempt. ICA's visa page does not list Norway as visa-required and says the stay is set by the Visit Pass issued; Norwegian MFA (page dated 23 May 2025, older) says normally up to 90 days; Wikipedia lists Norway in the 90-day group. Passport 6 months and funds/onward ticket come from the MFA and Wikipedia, not from the ICA pages read.

JP.name: Japan
JP.paperwork: Passport only. Visa-free up to 90 days. Visit Japan Web pre-registration is optional, not required.
JP.passport: Valid for the whole stay (MFA gives no minimum); emergency passport accepted
JP.atBorder: Immigration card and customs declaration (paper or Visit Japan Web); no fresh fruit, veg or meat
JP.notes: Norwegian MFA Japan (updated 20 Apr 2026): no visa for stays up to 90 days; Visit Japan Web pre-registration can ease entry but is optional; fresh fruit, vegetables and meat banned. Media (not official) report the departure tax rose from ¥1,000 to ¥3,000 (about €17) on 1 Jul 2026, collected in the airline ticket, and that the JESTA online travel authorisation is planned but not yet in force (Wikipedia: by 2030; media: law passed 29 May 2026). Japan's MOFA and Immigration Services Agency pages returned 403/404, so Japanese primary sources were not read. ID card not accepted.

KR.name: South Korea
KR.paperwork: Submit the free e-Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival. Norwegians are exempt from the K-ETA until 31 Dec 2026.
KR.passport: Valid for the whole stay; keep a blank page for the entry stamp
KR.atBorder: Nothing else for tourists; medicines with controlled substances need prior approval
KR.notes: Norwegian MFA Korea (updated 29 May 2026): Norway is temporarily exempt from K-ETA until 31 Dec 2026, visa-free 90 days, e-Arrival Card free. Korean Ministry of Justice notices: the temporary K-ETA exemption for currently exempt countries runs 1 Jan-31 Dec 2026 (list not on the notice; Norway per MFA and media list of 22 countries). A Dec 2026 trip is inside the window; if not extended, K-ETA (KRW 10,000, about €7) applies from 2027. K-ETA holders do not need to submit an arrival card. e-Arrival Card: official site says it can be filed from 3 days before arrival and is free; the MFA wording 'no later than 72 hours before arrival' conflicts with that. Whether a paper card remains available on arrival was not confirmed. ID card not accepted.

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.paperwork: Visa-free 45 days. Fill in the free Pre-Arrival Information declaration (prearrival.immigration.gov.vn) within 3 days before arrival.
VN.passport: Valid at least 6 months, counting the stay (MFA)
VN.atBorder: Show the declaration's confirmation QR code; e-cigarettes/vapes are banned
VN.notes: Visa exemption for Norway (and 11 other countries): 45 days from entry, valid 15 Mar 2025-14 Mar 2028 (Resolution 44/NQ-CP of 7 Mar 2025). Pre-Arrival Information (PAI) declaration: state broadcaster VTV says it is mandatory for foreigners entering Tan Son Nhat by air since 15 Apr 2026 and can be done on arrival via QR code; Singapore's embassy in Hanoi (25 Jun 2026) says it covers Noi Bai, Tan Son Nhat, Da Nang, Nha Trang and Phu Quoc but travellers are only 'encouraged'; Norwegian MFA (15 Jun 2026) asks arrivals at Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Phu Quoc to fill it in. Status varies by airport, so classified 'form' to be safe. Free on the official portal; avoid paid lookalike sites. The Vietnamese immigration portals returned certificate errors. ID card not accepted.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.paperwork: Visa on arrival at the airport, IDR 500,000 (about €25), or e-VOA online; also fill in the free All Indonesia arrival form.
ID.passport: Valid at least 6 months from planned departure, with 1+ blank page
ID.atBorder: Return ticket needed; Bali tourist levy IDR 150,000 (about €8) paid on arrival or at baliprov.go.id
ID.notes: Norwegian MFA Indonesia (updated 20 May 2026): B1 tourist visa (visa on arrival) at most entry points incl. Bali and Jakarta, IDR 500,000, 30 days, extendable once by 30 days (another IDR 500,000); can also be applied for online before arrival (e-VOA); electronic arrival card 'All Indonesia' (allindonesia.imigrasi.go.id) covering immigration, health and customs, earliest 3 days before arrival, no fee stated; overstay fine IDR 1,000,000 per day. Wikipedia agrees on fee, 30 days and 6-month passport. Indonesian immigration sites were not readable. ID card not accepted.

LK.name: Sri Lanka
LK.paperwork: Apply online for the Sri Lanka ETA (eta.gov.lk) before arrival; free for Norwegians since 25 May 2026; 30 days, double entry.
LK.passport: Valid at least 6 months from planned departure; emergency passport accepted
LK.atBorder: Show the approved ETA; private drones need Civil Aviation Authority permission
LK.notes: Official ETA site: from 25 May 2026 nationals of 40 countries (Norway is no. 25) get a free tourist visa/ETA, valid 30 days with double entry within those 30 days; an ETA must still be obtained before arrival. No end date for the scheme and no lead time are stated (applyDaysAhead is null); extensions cost the normal fee; fees paid before 25 May 2026 are non-refundable. Norwegian MFA (28 May 2026): tourists must apply for the ETA before arrival; passport valid six months from planned departure. Classified 'form' because it is free, but it is an authorisation that must be approved. ID card not accepted.

MV.name: Maldives
MV.paperwork: Submit the free Traveller Declaration online up to 96 hours before arrival. Free visa on arrival for up to 30 days.
MV.passport: Machine-readable, valid at least 1 month; emergency passports not accepted
MV.atBorder: Prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility, funds and return ticket may be checked
MV.notes: Maldives Immigration: all foreigners must submit the Traveller Declaration (free, one per traveller incl. children, up to 96 hours before arrival; avoid sites charging fees); tourist visa is granted on arrival; passport with MRZ and at least 1 month validity; itinerary must include a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility, sufficient funds and confirmed return tickets; a complete itinerary does not guarantee entry; no entry on Israeli passports since 15 Apr 2025. Norwegian MFA (1 Jun 2026): visa up to 30 days issued on arrival; alcohol import banned. 'Free' 30-day visa comes from Wikipedia (citing Maldives Immigration); the immigration page read does not state fee or length.

US.name: United States
US.paperwork: Apply for ESTA online at esta.cbp.dhs.gov (USD 40.27, about €36) before flying; valid 2 years; e-passport required.
US.passport: Valid e-passport (no emergency passports); the MFA gives no minimum validity
US.atBorder: Officers may ask to see your phone/devices and your plans; refusing can mean entry is denied
US.notes: Fee: USD 21 until Sep 2025, USD 40 from 30 Sep 2025, USD 40.27 from 1 Jan 2026 (US Embassy Singapore and the ESTA site, via search extracts; the embassy pages and esta.cbp.dhs.gov could not be fetched). CBP: ESTA can be submitted any time, preferably when you start planning or before buying tickets; no fixed minimum lead time is stated, so applyDaysAhead is null (older guidance reportedly said 72 hours); valid up to 2 years or until the passport expires; e-passport required; 90 days. CBP/DHS proposed on 10 Dec 2025 to make 5 years of social-media identifiers mandatory in ESTA; comments closed 9 Feb 2026 and no final rule or start date was found - US Embassy France said it was not yet in effect; check at application. Norwegian MFA (29 Jul 2026): border officers may request access to electronic devices; an I-94 record can be downloaded; emergency passports not allowed.

CA.name: Canada
CA.paperwork: Get a Canada eTA online (CAD 7, about €4) before you check in; air arrivals only; valid 5 years or until passport expires.
CA.passport: The same passport as on the eTA (it is linked to it); valid for the stay
CA.atBorder: May be asked for purpose, address and return ticket; customs entry form on arrival
CA.notes: IRCC: eTA costs CAD 7; most applicants are approved by email within minutes, but some requests take several days if documents are requested (no fixed lead time, so applyDaysAhead is null - apply when you book); valid up to five years or until the passport expires; stays normally up to six months; required only for air travel (not land or sea); linked to the passport used to apply. Norwegian MFA Canada (31 Jul 2026): eTA must be done online before check-in; Ebola-related entry measures for travellers from DR Congo, Uganda and South Sudan and a planned quarantine 30 May-29 Aug 2026 (past by Dec). ID card not accepted.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.paperwork: Passport only; up to 180 days without a visa. The immigration form (FMM) is issued at entry; its fee is in the air ticket.
MX.passport: Valid passport (MFA gives no minimum); you need the entry stamp to leave
MX.atBorder: Officer decides the days (not always 180); may ask for return ticket, lodging; customs form on entry
MX.notes: Norwegian MFA Mexico (updated 27 Feb 2026): up to 180 days without a visa, but not guaranteed - check the days on the entry stamp; the FMM immigration form and customs form are shown at entry; a passport with entry stamp is needed to exit. FMM fee 2026: MXN 983 (about €48) per Wikipedia and other secondary sources; airlines collect it with the ticket for air arrivals, so costEUR is 0 extra (not verified on the INM site). Digital FMM (FMMD) is used at major airports per secondary sources. ID card not accepted. INM site was not read.
